sources.name: The Gazette (insolvency notices)
sources.publisher: The Stationery Office for HM Government: the UK's official public record
sources.updates: Notices published every working day; desk reads the last 21 days daily
sources.stability: Long-running linked-data API (JSON/RDF per notice); occasional slow responses, retried
sources.issues: Notice text is submitted by insolvency practitioners and is legally checked; 'nature of business' is sometimes missing, so the sector may be inferred from the company name (labelled on the card).
sources.usedFor: Treasure hunter: company, notice type, date, postcode location, office-holder's published professional contact
sources.verdict: The authoritative source for UK insolvency events. Used as the backbone of the Treasure hunter desk.

sources.name: Companies House (company pages)
sources.issues: Filed data is self-reported by companies and not verified by Companies House. Linked only, not bulk-read (no API key yet).
sources.usedFor: Link from each Treasure lead to the company's filing history and SIC codes
sources.verdict: Official register. A free API key would let the desk read SIC codes directly and add dissolved heritage companies (see sign-ups).

sources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2
sources.licence: US Government work, no copyright restrictions on the records (terms ask that NLM is credited)
sources.issues: 'Why stopped' is free text written by sponsors and can be vague ('business decision'). Trials stopped for safety or efficacy are excluded by keyword, which can miss oddly worded ones.
sources.usedFor: Revival broker: trials stopped for funding or business reasons, and companies recruiting in the same condition
sources.verdict: Highly reliable registry. Leads are ranked below luxury and craft ones by design.

sources.name: UK IPO trade mark open data (Feb 2018 snapshot)
sources.updates: None since Feb 2018: the IPO paused bulk releases during its systems transformation
sources.stability: Static file; the live register blocks automated checks, so each lead must be verified by hand
sources.issues: Status is as of 2018. A mark marked dead may have been re-filed since. Marks that died before April 1996 aren't included. A lapsed mark can still carry goodwill.
sources.usedFor: Revival broker: 'sleeping beauty' marks in watches, jewellery, perfume, spirits, leather, tailoring, motoring, hotels and porcelain
sources.verdict: Official, but demoted for staleness. Every card says 'check before use' and links to the live register.

sources.name: Wikidata
sources.stability: SPARQL endpoint sometimes times out. The desk falls back to the last good copy and says so.
sources.issues: Coverage and accuracy vary. Missing 'replaced by' or 'owned by' statements can make a living brand look dormant. Leads are cross-checked against the UK mark snapshot and need human checks.
sources.usedFor: Revival broker (dissolved houses and marques); Import scout (descriptions)
sources.verdict: Good for discovery, not proof. Always paired with a 'check before use' note.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap name-suggestion-index
sources.stability: Versioned npm package served by jsDelivr
sources.issues: Lists brands that mappers have added. Small luxury ateliers are under-represented compared with chains.
sources.usedFor: Import scout: candidate brands and the countries they trade in
sources.verdict: Well-maintained, reviewed brand list. Fine for discovery.

sources.name: taginfo (worldwide and Geofabrik UK)
sources.issues: Counts reflect what is mapped, not reality. UK mapping is good for high streets but a brand may sell in the UK online or via stockists. The gap check is labelled accordingly.
sources.usedFor: Import scout: number of locations abroad, and UK presence check
sources.verdict: Reliable statistics on OSM. The UK-gap claim is limited to 'no mapped UK location'.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API
sources.stability: Public instances are often overloaded. The desk tries three, then skips nearby buyers for the day.
sources.issues: Business listings may be out of date or missing.
sources.usedFor: Treasure hunter: possible buyers nearby (distilleries, jewellers, boatyards…)
sources.verdict: Useful for buyer ideas only. Never used as a fact about the insolvent company.

sources.name: GitHub REST API
sources.licence: Public repository metadata under GitHub's terms. Code licences vary and are shown per lead.
sources.issues: Stars can be inflated. 'Archived' sometimes means 'moved to a new repo', so READMEs announcing a move are filtered out. Profile locations are self-reported.
sources.usedFor: Revival broker (archived or seeking-maintainer projects and active forks); Twin finder (maker sweeps)
sources.verdict: Accurate metadata. Self-reported fields are labelled as such.

sources.name: You're not the only one (mhccog)
sources.publisher: This project's sibling site; built from OpenAlex, arXiv, GitHub and Hacker News
sources.licence: Underlying: OpenAlex CC0, arXiv metadata CC0, GitHub/HN public metadata
sources.issues: Word-overlap matching in English can pair loosely related work. Locations are institution-level for papers.
sources.usedFor: Twin finder: research and project pairs across countries
sources.verdict: Reused with an added cross-country filter and a Crossref citation check.

sources.name: Crossref REST API
sources.issues: Reference lists are only open for some publishers, so 'not checked' is shown when they aren't.
sources.usedFor: Twin finder: do the two papers cite each other?

sources.name: Photon geocoder
sources.issues: Geocodes free-text GitHub profile locations, which can be vague or jokey. Precision is shown on the map.
sources.usedFor: Twin finder: placing makers by their stated location
sources.verdict: Approximate. Only used to place dots and to check the two sides are in different countries.

skipped.name: Participedia
skipped.why: Its CC BY-NC-SA licence forbids commercial use, and this desk is for fee-earning work.

skipped.name: OECD OPSI case library
skipped.why: The licence for reuse of the case texts isn't clearly open, so it's left out until confirmed.

skipped.name: Kickstarter / Product Hunt
skipped.why: No free, terms-compliant bulk access. Scraping would breach their terms.

skipped.name: Hackaday.io / open hardware sites
skipped.why: The API needs a key, and terms limit reuse. Open hardware is covered only where it's on GitHub.

skipped.name: EUIPO open data
skipped.why: Bulk data needs a registered account (free), so it's listed as a sign-up below rather than used.

skipped.name: Companies House bulk 'BasicCompanyData'
skipped.why: Only covers live companies (not dissolved heritage firms), and the Gazette notices already carry the nature of business. Kept for later.

skipped.name: Personal social profiles (LinkedIn, Instagram…)
skipped.why: Personal data beyond published professional contacts is out of scope (GDPR), and their terms forbid scraping.

skipped.name: Asset valuations
skipped.why: There's no open, reliable source. The desk shows asset appeal by sector and never invents a price.

signups.name: Companies House API
signups.why: Reads SIC codes and officers for every Gazette company, and finds dissolved heritage companies (pre-1950 incorporation, luxury SIC codes) for the Revival desk.

signups.name: OpenAlex API key
signups.why: Its own daily budget for finding who publishes on a stopped trial's drug, and fresher Twin finder research pairs.

signups.name: EUIPO open data
signups.why: EU trade mark statuses, to double-check sleeping-beauty names across Europe.
